cards.title: The strip has more than a name
cards.body: Flip it over. The foil and the box carry details that help you avoid mix-ups at home. Here's what to look for.

cards.title: Brand name and salt name
cards.body: The brand name is big. The actual ingredient, the salt, is usually smaller. Two different brands can contain the same salt.

cards.title: Strength
cards.body: Shown in mg or mcg. Same medicine, different strength is a common mix-up. Match it to the prescription every time.

cards.title: Batch number
cards.body: Useful if there's ever a quality question. Another reason to keep the strip until the last tablet is gone.

cards.title: Mfg and Exp dates
cards.body: Manufacture and expiry dates. Check the expiry before use, and don't cut the strip through it.

cards.title: Storage instructions
cards.body: "Store in a cool, dry place" or "protect from light". In a Lucknow May, the shelf next to the gas stove doesn't qualify.

cards.title: Read twice, swallow once
cards.body: If the strip doesn't match the prescription in name, salt or strength, ask your chemist before taking it.

takeaway: Check the salt, strength, expiry and storage on every strip, and ask the chemist if anything doesn't match the prescription.
share: Send this to the person who cuts strips into single tablets and loses the name.
